% hyperref's anchors as the first thing in a list, before its first
% \item or \bibitem: a \phantomsection under a heading, a \hypertarget,
% and a \phantomsection with the references' line in the table of
% contents. In the PDF, that line's link goes to the top of the list. On
% the page, the line links the heading right above the list. A
% \phantomsection right after an \item has its anchor in the item.
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage{hyperref}
\begin{document}
\tableofcontents
\section{One}
Text \cite{x}, items \ref{a} and \ref{q}, and \hyperlink{t}{the target}.
\begin{enumerate}
  \item \phantomsection\label{a} First.
  \item Second.
\end{enumerate}
\subsection{Two}
\begin{enumerate}
  \phantomsection\label{q}
  \item Third.
\end{enumerate}
Before the target.
\begin{enumerate}\hypertarget{t}{}\item Fourth.\end{enumerate}
\section*{Problems}
\phantomsection
\addcontentsline{toc}{section}{Problems}
\begin{enumerate}
  \item Alpha.
\end{enumerate}
\begin{thebibliography}{9}
  \phantomsection
  \addcontentsline{toc}{section}{\refname}
  \bibitem{x} A. Author. Title.
\end{thebibliography}
\end{document}
